chunks: 1491 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:

"Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He wishes to bring benefit through rain, He commands the clouds, so they take water from beneath the Throne; and when He does not intend vegetation, He commands the clouds, so they take water from the sea."
It was said: "The water of the sea is salty."
He said: "Indeed the clouds purify it."

key_terms.السَّحَابَ: the clouds that carry and draw water by Allah’s command
key_terms.النَّبَاتَ: vegetation or plant growth الناتج from rain
key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea, mentioned as another source of water
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, mentioned here as a source beneath which water is taken
key_terms.الْمَطَرِ: rain through which benefit is brought

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the source of rain and Allah’s control over vegetation?
ai.summary: This hadith describes rain as operating by the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and presents a distinction between water taken from beneath the Throne and water taken from the sea. It highlights divine control over natural processes and connects rainfall with benefit and vegetation by Allah’s will.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1491 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Him (as) that He said:

"When Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, wishes to bring benefit through rain, He commands the clouds to take water from beneath the Throne. But when He does not intend for vegetation to grow, He commands the clouds to take water from the sea."
It was said: "But sea water is salty."
